title: GST 114 ( UNN ) : CHAPTER SIX ( CONCORD IN SENTENCE )
subject: GST 114

questions.question: Concord in sentence construction is primarily concerned with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Okoye defines concord as the agreement between words in a sentence.

questions.question: Which type of concord is based on grammatical rules rather than meaning?
questions.explanation: Grammatical concord follows strict rules of grammar rather than intended meaning.

questions.question: The concept of concord refers to which of the following?
questions.explanation: The concept of concord refers to sentence agreement as discussed by Okoye.

questions.question: Which type of concord emphasizes the meaning of the subject over its grammatical form?
questions.explanation: Notional concord prioritizes the intended meaning over strict grammar.

questions.question: Which type of concord is also referred to as attraction concord?
questions.explanation: Proximity concord is also known as attraction concord.

questions.question: A singular subject takes a singular verb under which rule?
questions.explanation: Rule 1 states that a singular subject takes a singular verb.

questions.question: A compound subject joined by 'and' takes which type of verb?
questions.explanation: A compound subject joined by 'and' takes a plural verb.

questions.question: In the sentence "The committee has decided", the verb is singular because the committee acts as which entity?
questions.explanation: The committee acts as a single unit, hence the singular verb.

questions.question: "Ten thousand naira is a lot of money" follows which rule of concord?
questions.explanation: Nouns of amount take singular verbs.

questions.question: The title of a book, even if plural in form, takes which type of verb?
questions.explanation: Titles of books take singular verbs regardless of their form.

questions.question: Which rule governs the sentence "The committee arrive tomorrow"?
questions.explanation: Collective nouns can take plural verbs when members act individually.

questions.question: "The governor, accompanied by his wife, is here" follows which rule?
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the main subject, not the intervening phrase.

questions.question: Subjects connected by "either... or" take a verb according to which element?
questions.explanation: With correlative conjunctions, the verb agrees with the nearer subject.

questions.question: Indefinite pronouns like "everyone" or "each" typically take which type of verb?
questions.explanation: Indefinite pronouns like everyone take singular verbs.

questions.question: Which rule applies when a relative pronoun is the subject?
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the antecedent of the relative pronoun.

questions.question: "In the jungle roar the lions" is an example of which rule?
questions.explanation: Rule 11 covers inverted subject-verb order.

questions.question: Subjects modified by "each" or "every" take which type of verb?
questions.explanation: Distributive adjectives take singular verbs.

questions.question: "Many a student has failed" follows which rule?
questions.explanation: "Many a" takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Which phrase takes a plural verb?
questions.explanation: "A number of" takes a plural verb.

questions.question: "The number of students is increasing" follows which pattern?
questions.explanation: "The number of" takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Nouns like "news" and "physics" take which type of verb?
questions.explanation: Subjects plural in form but singular in sense take singular verbs.

questions.question: Adjectives used as nouns like "the rich" take which verb?
questions.explanation: Adjectives used as nouns referring to a class take plural verbs.

questions.question: "The teacher, together with the students, is here" follows which rule?
questions.explanation: Intervening expressions do not affect the verb.

questions.question: "Two hundred naira is the price" follows which rule?
questions.explanation: Plural nouns expressing a single amount take singular verbs.

questions.question: Subjects joined by "or" or "nor" take a verb according to which principle?
questions.explanation: With "or" and "nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject.

questions.question: A shift in tense occurs when a writer does which of the following?
questions.explanation: Shifting tense without reason creates inconsistency.

questions.question: A shift in voice occurs when a writer does which of the following?
questions.explanation: Shifting from active to passive voice unnecessarily is a voice shift.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates a shift in tense?
questions.explanation: Mixing past and present tense creates a shift.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates a shift in voice?
options: He ate and food was eaten
The food was eaten by the boy
The boy is eating the food
questions.explanation: Mixing active and passive voice creates a shift.

questions.question: The sentence "The committee have decided" is corrected by changing "have" to which word?
questions.explanation: The committee acts as a single unit, so it takes the singular verb "is".

questions.question: "Neither of the boys are coming" is corrected by changing "are" to which word?
questions.explanation: "Neither" is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.question: "Ten thousand naira are a lot of money" is corrected by changing "are" to which word?
questions.explanation: Nouns of amount take singular verbs.

questions.question: "The number of students are increasing" is corrected by changing "are" to which word?
questions.explanation: "The number of" takes a singular verb.

questions.question: "A number of students is absent" is corrected by changing "is" to which word?
questions.explanation: "A number of" takes a plural verb.

questions.question: "Each of the boys have a book" is corrected by changing "have" to which word?
questions.explanation: "Each" is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.question: "Many a student have passed" is corrected by changing "have" to which word?
questions.explanation: "Many a" takes a singular verb.

questions.question: "The news are bad" is corrected by changing "are" to which word?
questions.explanation: "News" is singular in sense and takes a singular verb.

questions.question: "The rich is not always happy" is corrected by changing "is" to which word?
questions.explanation: "The rich" takes a plural verb.

questions.question: "Either of the girls are coming" is corrected by changing "are" to which word?
questions.explanation: "Either" is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.question: "The teacher with the students are here" is corrected by changing "are" to which word?
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the main subject "teacher".

questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: When acting as a single unit, the committee takes a singular verb.

options: Ten thousand naira are a lot

Ten thousand naira were a lot
Ten thousand naira be a lot
questions.explanation: Nouns of amount take singular verbs.

options: The number of students are increasing
The number of students is increasing
The number of students were increasing
The number of students be increasing
questions.explanation: "The number of" takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: A number of students is absent
A number of students are absent
A number of students was absent
A number of students be absent
questions.explanation: "A number of" takes a plural verb.

questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Each of the boys have a book
Each of the boys has a book
Each of the boys are having a book
Each of the boys were having a book
questions.explanation: "Each" is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: "Many a" takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: "News" is singular in sense and takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: The rich is not always happy
The rich are not always happy
The rich was not always happy
The rich be not always happy
questions.explanation: "The rich" takes a plural verb.

questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Neither of the boys are coming
Neither of the boys is coming
Neither of the boys were coming
Neither of the boys be coming
questions.explanation: "Neither" is singular and takes a singular verb.

questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: The teacher with the students are here
The teacher with the students is here
The teacher with the students were here
The teacher with the students be here
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the main subject "teacher".
